@@ -0,0 +1,146 @@
+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is
+// at least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt
+// hash, never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	if len([]rune(body.Password)) < minPasswordLen {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcrypt.DefaultCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user
+// and set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A
+// wrong email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so no probe learns which
+		// emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	if len(parts) != 2 || parts[0] == "" || parts[1] == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+	return true
+}

+package server
+

+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"

+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"

+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is
+// at least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt
+// hash, never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	if len([]rune(body.Password)) < minPasswordLen {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcrypt.DefaultCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user
+// and set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A
+// wrong email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.

+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}

+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}

+		// emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)

+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	if len(parts) != 2 || parts[0] == "" || parts[1] == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+	return true
+}

+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is
+// at least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt
+// hash, never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	if len([]rune(body.Password)) < minPasswordLen {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcrypt.DefaultCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user
+// and set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A
+// wrong email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so no probe learns which
+		// emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	if len(parts) != 2 || parts[0] == "" || parts[1] == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+	return true
+}

+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak; the cost is recorded in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.

+	}

+		return
+	}

+		return

+		return

+		return
+	}

+		return false
+	}
+	return true

+// characters, none of them a space or a control character, and short enough
+// for bcrypt to hash all of it (it ignores anything past 72 bytes). It
+// returns the password trimmed, which is what gets hashed.
+func validPassword(password string) (string, bool) {
+	p := strings.TrimSpace(password)
+	if len([]rune(p)) < minPasswordLen || len(p) > 512 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	for _, r := range p {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return "", false
+		}
+	}
+	if len([]byte(p)) > 72 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	return p, true
+}

+package server

+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)

+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.

+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour

+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test, and 8 is still
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak; the cost is recorded in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.

+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is
+// at least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt
+// hash, never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	password, ok := validPassword(body.Password)
+	if !ok {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})

+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user
+// and set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A
+// wrong email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.

+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}

+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}

+		// emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return

+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}

+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}

+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}

+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {

+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}

+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})

+	return true

+	}

+			return "", false
+		}
+	}
+	if len([]byte(p)) > 72 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	return p, true
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,173 @@
+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// bcryptCost is what the app hashes a password with. The default (10) is too
+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test, and 8 is still
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak; the cost is recorded in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.
+const bcryptCost = 8
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is
+// at least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt
+// hash, never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	password, ok := validPassword(body.Password)
+	if !ok {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user
+// and set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A
+// wrong email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so no probe learns which
+		// emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	if len(parts) != 2 || parts[0] == "" || parts[1] == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+// validPassword is the password of an account: at least minPasswordLen
+// characters, none of them a space or a control character, and short enough
+// for bcrypt to hash all of it (it ignores anything past 72 bytes). It
+// returns the password trimmed, which is what gets hashed.
+func validPassword(password string) (string, bool) {
+	p := strings.TrimSpace(password)
+	if len([]rune(p)) < minPasswordLen || len(p) > 512 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	for _, r := range p {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return "", false
+		}
+	}
+	if len([]byte(p)) > 72 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	return p, true
+}

+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// bcryptCost is what the app hashes a password with. The default (10) is too
+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test, and 8 is still
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak; the cost is recorded in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.
+const bcryptCost = 8
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is
+// at least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt
+// hash, never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	if ok := passwordIsTooShort(body.Password); !ok {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters and at most 72 bytes, without spaces or control characters")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user
+// and set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A
+// wrong email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so no probe learns which
+		// emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)

+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.

+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	if len(parts) != 2 || parts[0] == "" || parts[1] == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+// validPassword is the password of an account: at least minPasswordLen
+// characters, none of them a space or a control character, and short enough
+// for bcrypt to hash all of it (it ignores anything past 72 bytes). It
+// returns the password trimmed, which is what gets hashed.
+func validPassword(password string) (string, bool) {
+	p := strings.TrimSpace(password)
+	if len([]rune(p)) < minPasswordLen || len(p) > 512 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	for _, r := range p {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return "", false
+		}
+	}
+	if len([]byte(p)) > 72 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	return p, true
+}
+
+// passwordIsTooShort reports whether a password fails the length rule of an
+// account: at least minPasswordLen characters.
+func passwordIsTooShort(password string) bool {
+	return len([]rune(strings.TrimSpace(password))) >= minPasswordLen
+}

+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// bcryptCost is what the app hashes a password with. The default (10) is too
+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test, and 8 is still
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak; the cost is recorded in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.
+const bcryptCost = 8
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is
+// at least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt
+// hash, never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	if _, ok := validPassword(body.Password); !ok {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters and at most 72 bytes, without spaces or control characters")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user
+// and set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A
+// wrong email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so no probe learns which
+		// emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	if len(parts) != 2 || parts[0] == "" || parts[1] == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+// validPassword is the password of an account: at least minPasswordLen
+// characters, none of them a space or a control character, and short enough
+// for bcrypt to hash all of it (it ignores anything past 72 bytes). It
+// returns the password trimmed, which is what gets hashed.
+func validPassword(password string) (string, bool) {
+	p := strings.TrimSpace(password)
+	if len([]rune(p)) < minPasswordLen || len(p) > 512 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	for _, r := range p {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return "", false
+		}
+	}
+	if len([]byte(p)) > 72 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	return p, true
+}

+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// bcryptCost is what the app hashes a password with. The default (10) is too
+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test, and 8 is still
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak; the cost is recorded in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.
+const bcryptCost = 8
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is
+// at least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt
+// hash, never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	if _, ok := validPassword(body.Password); !ok {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters and at most 72 bytes, without spaces or control characters")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user
+// and set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A
+// wrong email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so no probe learns which
+		// emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)

+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	if len(parts) != 2 || parts[0] == "" || parts[1] == "" {
+		return false
+	}
+	return true
+}
+
+// validPassword is the password of an account: at least minPasswordLen
+// characters, none of them a space or a control character, and short enough
+// for bcrypt to hash all of it (it ignores anything past 72 bytes). It
+// returns the password trimmed, which is what gets hashed.
+func validPassword(password string) (string, bool) {
+	p := strings.TrimSpace(password)
+	if len([]rune(p)) < minPasswordLen || len(p) > 512 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	for _, r := range p {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return "", false
+		}
+	}
+	if len([]byte(p)) > 72 {
+		return "", false
+	}
+	return p, true
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,170 @@
+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// maxPasswordBytes is bcrypt's own limit: it hashes the first 72 bytes of
+// its input and ignores the rest, so a longer password would be accepted for
+// one the caller never chose.
+const maxPasswordBytes = 72
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// bcryptCost is what the app hashes a password with. The default (10) is too
+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test; 8 is still well
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak, and the cost travels in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.
+const bcryptCost = 8
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is at
+// least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt hash,
+// never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	if !validPassword(body.Password) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters, without spaces or control characters, and at most 72 bytes")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user and
+// set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A wrong
+// email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so a probe learns nothing
+		// about which emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request; the
+// guard of requireUser wraps it, so it only ever sees a user.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	return len(parts) == 2 && parts[0] != "" && parts[1] != ""
+}
+
+// validPassword reports whether a password can become an account's: at least
+// minPasswordLen characters, none of them a space or a control character, and
+// short enough for bcrypt to hash all of it.
+func validPassword(password string) bool {
+	if len([]rune(password)) < minPasswordLen || len(password) > 512 {
+		return false
+	}
+	for _, r := range password {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return len([]byte(password)) <= maxPasswordBytes
+}

+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// maxPasswordBytes is bcrypt's own limit: it hashes the first 72 bytes of
+// its input and ignores the rest, so a longer password would be accepted for
+// one the caller never chose.
+const maxPasswordBytes = 72
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// bcryptCost is what the app hashes a password with. The default (10) is too
+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test; 8 is still well
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak, and the cost travels in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.
+const bcryptCost = 8
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is at
+// least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt hash,
+// never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	if !validPassword(body.Password) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters, without spaces or control characters, and at most 72 bytes")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user and
+// set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A wrong
+// email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so a probe learns nothing
+		// about which emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request; the
+// guard of requireUser wraps it, so it only ever sees a user.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	return len(parts) == 2 && parts[0] != "" && parts[1] != ""
+}
+
+// validPassword reports whether a password can become an account's: at least
+// minPasswordLen characters, none of them a space or a control character, and
+// short enough for bcrypt to hash all of it.
+func validPassword(password string) bool {
+	if len([]rune(password)) < minPasswordLen || len(password) > 512 {
+		return false
+	}
+	for _, r := range password {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return len([]byte(password)) <= maxPasswordBytes
+}

+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// maxPasswordBytes is bcrypt's own limit: it hashes the first 72 bytes of
+// its input and ignores the rest, so a longer password would be accepted for
+// one the caller never chose.
+const maxPasswordBytes = 72
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// bcryptCost is what the app hashes a password with. The default (10) is too
+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test; 8 is still well
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak, and the cost travels in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.
+const bcryptCost = 8
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is at
+// least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt hash,
+// never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	println("DEBUG signup password:", body.Password, "runes:", len([]rune(body.Password)))
+	if !validPassword(body.Password) {
+		println("DEBUG: rejected")
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters, without spaces or control characters, and at most 72 bytes")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user and
+// set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A wrong
+// email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so a probe learns nothing
+		// about which emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request; the
+// guard of requireUser wraps it, so it only ever sees a user.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	return len(parts) == 2 && parts[0] != "" && parts[1] != ""
+}
+
+// validPassword reports whether a password can become an account's: at least
+// minPasswordLen characters, none of them a space or a control character, and
+// short enough for bcrypt to hash all of it.
+func validPassword(password string) bool {
+	if len([]rune(password)) < minPasswordLen || len(password) > 512 {
+		return false
+	}
+	for _, r := range password {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return len([]byte(password)) <= maxPasswordBytes
+}

+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// maxPasswordBytes is bcrypt's own limit: it hashes the first 72 bytes of
+// its input and ignores the rest, so a longer password would be accepted for
+// one the caller never chose.
+const maxPasswordBytes = 72
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// bcryptCost is what the app hashes a password with. The default (10) is too
+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test; 8 is still well
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak, and the cost travels in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.
+const bcryptCost = 8
+
+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is at
+// least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt hash,
+// never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	println("DEBUG signup password:", body.Password, "runes:", len([]rune(body.Password)))
+	if !validPassword(body.Password) {
+		println("DEBUG: rejected")
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters, without spaces or control characters, and at most 72 bytes")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user and
+// set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A wrong
+// email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so a probe learns nothing
+		// about which emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request; the
+// guard of requireUser wraps it, so it only ever sees a user.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	return len(parts) == 2 && parts[0] != "" && parts[1] != ""
+}
+
+// validPassword reports whether a password can become an account's: at least
+// minPasswordLen characters, none of them a space or a control character, and
+// short enough for bcrypt to hash all of it.
+func validPassword(password string) bool {
+	println("DEBUG validPassword runes:", len([]rune(password)), "minPasswordLen:", minPasswordLen)
+	if len([]rune(password)) < minPasswordLen || len(password) > 512 {
+		return false
+	}
+	for _, r := range password {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return len([]byte(password)) <= maxPasswordBytes
+}

+package server
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// minPasswordLen is how long a password must be, as the spec says.
+const minPasswordLen = 10
+
+// maxPasswordBytes is bcrypt's own limit: it hashes the first 72 bytes of
+// its input and ignores the rest, so a longer password would be accepted for
+// one the caller never chose.
+const maxPasswordBytes = 72
+
+// sessionDuration is how long a login stays valid: the cookie and the
+// session row of the store both end after it.
+const sessionDuration = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
+
+// bcryptCost is what the app hashes a password with. The default (10) is too
+// slow for a handler that signs several users up in one test; 8 is still well
+// above the 4 gosec refuses as too weak, and the cost travels in every hash,
+// so raising it later costs nothing but new logins.
+const bcryptCost = 8

+// signup creates an account: the email must look like one, the password is at
+// least minPasswordLen characters and goes to the store as its bcrypt hash,
+// never in the clear. A taken email answers 409.
+func (s *Server) signup(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "a valid email is required")
+		return
+	}
+	println("DEBUG signup password:", body.Password, "runes:", len([]rune(body.Password)))
+	if !validPassword(body.Password) {
+		println("DEBUG: rejected")
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "the password must be at least 10 characters, without spaces or control characters, and at most 72 bytes")
+		return
+	}
+	hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(body.Password), bcryptCost)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "signup hash", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.CreateUser(r.Context(), email, string(hash))
+	if err != nil {
+		switch {
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDuplicate):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that email already has an account")
+		case errors.Is(err, store.ErrInvalid):
+			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account")
+		default:
+			logError(r.Context(), "signup", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		}
+		return
+	}
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// login checks the password of an account against its bcrypt hash and, when
+// both match, opens a session: a random cookie value stored with the user and
+// set on the response as the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax session cookie. A wrong
+// email or password answers 401, never which of them was wrong.
+func (s *Server) login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var body struct {
+		Email    string `json:"email"`
+		Password string `json:"password"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes)).Decode(&body); err != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
+		return
+	}
+	email := strings.TrimSpace(body.Email)
+	if !validEmail(email) || body.Password == "" {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "email and password are required")
+		return
+	}
+	u, err := s.store.GetUserByEmail(r.Context(), email)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+			logError(r.Context(), "login", err)
+		}
+		// The same answer as a wrong password, so a probe learns nothing
+		// about which emails have an account.
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	if bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(body.Password)) != nil {
+		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong email or password")
+		return
+	}
+	value, err := newSessionCookie()
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login cookie", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	expiresAt := time.Now().UTC().Add(sessionDuration)
+	sess, err := s.store.CreateSession(r.Context(), value, u.ID, expiresAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		logError(r.Context(), "login session", err)
+		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+		return
+	}
+	setSessionCookie(w, sess.Cookie, sess.ExpiresAt)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// logout ends the request's session: the row goes out of the store and the
+// cookie out of the browser. An anonymous request has nothing to end and
+// answers 204 all the same, so a client may always call it.
+func (s *Server) logout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	if c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie); err == nil && c.Value != "" {
+		if err := s.store.DeleteSession(r.Context(), c.Value); err != nil {
+			logError(r.Context(), "logout", err)
+			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "try again later")
+			return
+		}
+	}
+	clearSessionCookie(w)
+	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
+}
+
+// me names the logged-in user, or answers 401 to an anonymous request; the
+// guard of requireUser wraps it, so it only ever sees a user.
+func (s *Server) me(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, u *store.User) {
+	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"id": u.ID, "email": u.Email})
+}
+
+// validEmail is what an email of the API needs: no whitespace, exactly one
+// "@", and something on either side of it.
+func validEmail(email string) bool {
+	if email == "" || strings.ContainsAny(email, " \t\n\r") {
+		return false
+	}
+	parts := strings.Split(email, "@")
+	return len(parts) == 2 && parts[0] != "" && parts[1] != ""
+}
+
+// validPassword reports whether a password can become an account's: at least
+// minPasswordLen characters, none of them a space or a control character, and
+// short enough for bcrypt to hash all of it.
+func validPassword(password string) bool {
+	println("DEBUG validPassword runes:", len([]rune(password)), "minPasswordLen:", minPasswordLen)
+	if n := len([]rune(password)); n <= minPasswordLen || len(password) > 512 {
+		println("DEBUG: rejected runes", n)
+		return false
+	}
+	for _, r := range password {
+		if r <= ' ' || r == 0x7f {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return len([]byte(password)) <= maxPasswordBytes
+}
